nom: SUNDAY RILEY Aquamarine Melt Hydrating Gel Balm Cleanser

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin are mixed: some say it works well and controls oil for oily or combination skin, while others found it left a greasy film or caused breakouts.
segments.dry: The dry-skin reports are more positive, including one detailed account of it finally working after sensitive-skincare and Korean routines failed, though one reviewer found it drying rather than hydrating for her dry skin.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers are divided: some report no irritation and gentle cleansing over weeks, while others, including one who developed breakouts and clogged pores, found it didn't suit their sensitive or acne-prone skin.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers are split between those who find it effective and those who found it stripped their skin of moisture and left it feeling dry and tight.
segments.normal: The one reviewer who describes normal skin reports the product caused acne breakouts for her, and she suspects it would not suit oily or combination skin either.

concerns.dehydration: Several reviewers report the balm-to-oil formula leaves skin hydrated without stripping it, but others, including some with dry or combination skin, found it left their skin feeling stripped, dry, and tight afterward.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer with dry skin specifically credits the formula with leaving enough moisture behind to avoid stripping her skin barrier, after other gentle skincare routines had failed her.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers report no new breakouts, but at least two, including one with sensitive/acne-prone skin and one with normal skin, report breakouts or clogged pores after use.
concerns.oiliness: Reports on residue are mixed: several reviewers, including one with sensitive skin, say it leaves an oily or greasy film on the face, while others, including reviewers who describe their skin as oily or combination, say it controls oil well and rinses clean.

aspects.libelle: Gel that melts into an oil, then rinses into a milk
Strong or divisive scent, described as rubbery or earthy
Pump can be difficult, clogged, or unpredictable
Doesn't fully remove heavy or waterproof makeup on its own
Considered expensive for what it delivers

extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] The packaging is pretty and appealing. The bottle was kind of hard to open. The actual product smelled so bad I didn't even want to try it. When I did try it, it made my face feel so awful. It was way too oily and I almost couldn't wash it off. It made my skin feel really gross and even after I washed my face again I could still smell the product. 10/10 do NOT recommend

extraits.titre: Not for me, pleasant scent, though
extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] The Sunday Riley Aquamarine Melt Hydrating Gel-Balm Cleanser was a no-go for me. I loved the scent of this cleanser, and it could be good when you just feel too lazy to do a good thorough face cleansing. However, for the price, I can't say this cleanser is any better than any other oil cleanser out on the market, and I feel it needs to be followed up with an actual soap cleanser. I also don't think this cleanser will work for anyone who has oily skin or combination skin. I think it caused acne breakouts on my skin as well, and I have normal skin. Therefore, I won't be using it again.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] I wanted to love this cleanser but unfortunately I didn't. The packaging is pretty nice. The pump nozzle was easy to use. There really isn't a noticeable scent. the consistency was a lot thinner than I anticipated and I felt like my skin was stripped of all moisture after use. I didn't really get the feel that it goes from balm to oil. I would have to follow-up with another cleanser as this was felt like my skin was overly dry after use leaving it feeling "tight" despite containing cocoa butter, evening primrose oil and malachite, this did not work well on my combination skin. I would use this as a makeup remover cleanser follow-up up by a second cleanser.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] The packaging of this product makes it very easy and mess free to use. The consistency is great and melts into face. The smell is nice but very strong. I have sensitive skin and the product doesn't irritate my skin, however it does leave my skin feeling oily. I noticed some breakouts and clogged pores after using this product multiple days in a row.

extraits.titre: A long awaited solution to my dry skin
extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] Before Sunday Riley's Aquamarine Melt Gel-Balm Cleanser, I would run to my moisturizer after washing my face to mitigate an uncomfortable, tight, and parched feeling. Sensitive skincare didn't work. Nor did Korean nor Vanicream. I had devolved to not washing my face at all. But THIS. This wash is something I LOOK FORWARD to using. The product itself does not foam and isn't cream, but is not overly oily. It's a…fluffy oil - like if you used an immersion blender on a lip mask. I rub 2 pumps onto my dry face and remove with a soft warm washcloth. It feels like I'm leaving a tad of the oil behind - but it truly does MELT into your skin, leaving behind an adequate amount of moisture so as not to strip your skin's barrier. It leaves my skin bright and able to receive moisturizer without burning. The label encourages one to breathe in the essential oils of it - one being a hint of refreshing chamomile, not a hit-you-in-face scent of lavender, peppermint, or tea tree (ones might also irritate your delicate skin barrier). Though I am someone who could blissfully live in a bottle of essential oils, the smell of this is beautifully subtle. My one and only gripe with this is the packaging. The tapered base in combination with a loose fitting cap (and me not wearing my contacts when I wash my face), has led to me knocking this over and blurrily chasing the top as it bounces around the bathroom floor 4 out of 5 times.
